about: Engines (DESIGN 5.11): processing modules compiled once to WebAssembly that every stack hosts alike. An engine is a plain WebAssembly module that exports its `memory`, `clarity_alloc(len) -> place` and `clarity_free(place, len)`, and each of its functions under its own name as `(place, len) -> i64`. To call one, the host writes the arguments as a JSON array (UTF-8) into room from clarity_alloc and calls the function with its place and length; the engine takes that room over. The function gives the place and length of its answer packed in an i64 (place in the high 32 bits), `{"value": ...}` or `{"error": "why"}`, which the host reads and gives back with clarity_free. Values are JSON as everywhere in Clarity: integers as numbers, decimals and money as exact text, enums by name, records as objects of their fields. An engine imports only the services of Clarity it declares with `uses` (`uses`), from module `clarity`: `clock() -> i64` (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), `random() -> i64` (the next number of splitmix64, seeded afresh for every call), and `log(place, len)` (a line of UTF-8 text, which the host writes to the application's log as `engine <Name>: <text>`). A host refuses a module that imports anything else, that is no WebAssembly, or that lacks the interface or a declared function, when it loads it. `engine` is test.wasm, built from engines/test. Each engine has limits per call (`limits`: seconds and megabytes). A call that runs longer than its time limit is stopped by the host and fails with exactly `engine <Name> failed in <function>: it ran longer than <n> second(s)`. An engine never gets more memory than its memory limit; growing past it fails as the engine's own allocator reports, most often as a failure of the call, `engine <Name> failed in <function>: ...` in the host's words. `limited` lists calls under the file's limits: `gives` an answer, or `fails` with a message that starts as given. `services` fixes the clock and the seed for `served`, the calls of the services; `log` lists the lines a call writes. A refused case loads with the file's `uses` unless it gives its own.
